paper.title: Automated Design of Agentic Systems
paper.central_claim: ADAS automates invention of agentic building blocks and workflows in code. Meta Agent Search iteratively programs novel agents conditioned on a scored archive, greatly outperforming hand-designed agents across multiple domains and transferring robustly across domains and foundation models.

evidence.quote: The core idea of Meta Agent Search is to adopt FMs as meta agents to iteratively program interestingly new agents based on an ever-growing archive of previous discoveries.
evidence.support_explanation: Proposer conditions on retained designs; code is the non-weight search object.

evidence.quote: (3) The generated agent is evaluated using validation data from the target domain. If errors occur during evaluation, the meta agent performs a self-reflection step to refine the design, repeating this process up to five times if necessary. (4) Finally, the agent is added to the archive along with its evaluation metrics, and the process continues with the updated archive until the maximum number of iterations is reached.
evidence.support_explanation: Execution/validation feedback, bounded debug, archive persistence and later search are operationally explicit; archive contains scored designs rather than only independently certified winners.

evidence.quote: For GPQA (Science), we use GPQA_diamond and the validation set consists of 32 questions, while the remaining 166 questions form the test set. G.reason: Concrete whole-workflow manual-design gap and clear tool/prompt-search distinction; direct FunSearch/OPRO original audit remains unresolved.

M.reason: Archive-conditioned code proposal, objective feedback and bounded debugging are operationally clear; open representation does not guarantee effective coverage.

X.reason: Full prompts/framework/pseudocode, models/splits and update schedule specified; displayed best-agent constructor/call mismatch and no isolated archive utility prevent stronger execution confidence.

E.measurement.reason: Exact grid/answer accuracy and DROP F1 are relevant objective outcome measures with denominators and bootstrap intervals; cross-design answer-parsing effects lack independent audit. Source-test selection is scored under holdout, not measurement.

E.causality.reason: Strong manual/prompt baselines and empty-initialization ablation; archive-off and matched search/deployment compute controls absent.

E.holdout.reason: Explicit validation/test splits and frozen cross-domain/executor transfers, but ARC top3 test selection and no overlap audit weaken strongest holdout claim.

E.statistics.reason: Test bootstrap intervals and repeated executions meet frozen A2 level2; no repeated independent search seeds, intervals and significance combination.

E.cost.reason: Approximate full search/evaluation dollars are reported; no complete per-agent inference/latency ledger, equal-budget comparison or amortization frontier.

signatures.object: Executable AgentSystem.forward workflow, prompts, roles and module interactions; backbone weights and meta-agent prompts fixed
signatures.information: Archive of previous agent code/descriptions and validation metrics; task examples and execution/runtime feedback
signatures.operation: Generate thought/name/code, perform two novelty/implementation self-reflections, evaluate, debug runtime errors up to five times, archive design and metrics, repeat
signatures.output: Runnable agent workflow code and scored archive entries
signatures.conditions: Programmable FM interface, target-domain validation set, execution infrastructure and adequate offline search budget
signatures.feedback: Objective task success/F1/accuracy and runtime-error traces
signatures.selection_rule: Archive scored candidates, not just accepted improvements; choose high-performing designs after fixed search; ARC transfer top3 ranked by source-test performance
signatures.selection_data: 20 ARC validation questions or 32 GPQA /128 other-domain validation questions; source test influences ARC top selection
signatures.persistence: Expanding scored archive conditions subsequent proposals; selected code reused unchanged across later test instances and transferred executors
signatures.later_use: Held-out problems, transferred domains and foundation models
signatures.claimed_effect: Novel agents outperform manually designed systems and generalize robustly
signatures.failure_boundary: Small validation sets, search cost, test-based ranking, executor/task-specific effects, uncertain exact displayed-code execution

gap.author_gap: Agent research manually invents both building blocks and workflows, restricting automation to narrow predefined spaces.
gap.checked_gap: Concrete residual is making entire executable workflow code searchable, with scored historical designs informing new proposals; not merely optimizing a prompt or tool inventory.

gap.closest_adjacent: FunSearch supplies archive-conditioned program synthesis; OPRO is directly compared. AgentOptimizer updates tools and Symbolic Learning edits configs, whereas ADAS searches whole forward workflows. Independent originality against FunSearch cannot be closed without its fixed original.
gap.residue: Code representational openness does not guarantee search coverage, novelty, safe execution or reliable validation generalization.
gap.stakes: Reusable agent orchestration could replace manual workflow engineering for a target distribution.
gap.method_response: Meta-agent writes complete forward code using simple FM interface and a scored archive.
gap.remaining_gap: No matched-budget archive-off isolation; no repeated independent search variance; source-test ranking and inconsistent cross-domain/model superiority restrict universal transfer claim.
unresolved: Request fixed FunSearch and OPRO originals in shared package to close nearest-neighbor program-search novelty audit; no private external fetch.

claims.text: Meta Agent Search discovers better agents across multiple domains
claims.setting: gpt-4o-2024-05-13 meta-agent; gpt-3.5-turbo-0125 executor; ARC and DROP/MGSM/MMLU/GPQA
claims.baseline_control: CoT, CoT-SC N5, Self-Refine≤5, Debate2, Quality-Diversity3, Step-back, RoleAssignment, OPRO; AppendixI empty archive initialization
claims.selection_vs_test: Validation scores drive search; every ARC design also test-evaluated; top ARC designs explicitly chosen by test accuracy
claims.result_denominator: Table1 DROP79.4±0.8 vs best handcrafted65.8±0.9; MGSM53.4±3.5 vs39.0±3.4; MMLU69.6±3.2 vs65.9±3.2; GPQA34.6±3.2 vs31.6±3.2. ARC20val/60test×5; GPQA32val/166test×5; other domains128val/800test×1.
claims.counterevidence: MMLU/GPQA confidence intervals overlap baselines. Empty initialization gives MGSM67.5±3.3 vs seeded53.4±3.5, so initialization value is not monotonic. Baseline and discovered design inference compute not matched.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Author-reported full-recipe held-out gains, especially DROP and math; no isolated archive-causal or uniformly significant superiority claim.

claims.text: Discovered agents transfer robustly across domains and foundation models
claims.setting: Top3 MGSM workflows transferred to GSM8K/GSM-Hard/MMLU/DROP and appendix tasks; top3 ARC agents across GPT/Claude executors
claims.baseline_control: Same framework hand-designed baselines on target tasks and models
claims.selection_vs_test: Frozen code transfer; ARC candidates selected by source-test performance; no pretraining/family-overlap audit
claims.result_denominator: Table2 best MGSM-derived design GSM8K69.5 vs strongest baseline43.6 and GSM-Hard31.2 vs18.0. DynamicRolePlaying MMLU62.4 vs baseline65.9; AppendixA transferred GPQA28.6/28.7/29.9 vs SelfRefine31.6. ARC Haiku one agent5.0 vs SelfRefine6.3, Sonnet one38.7 vs39.3.
claims.counterevidence: Several non-math/model cells fail universal superiority; large math transfer gains do not resolve shared-family contamination or source-test selection.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Substantial scoped cross-task/model reuse, not every agent beating every baseline.

claims.text: ADAS opens a route to recursively improving agent designers
claims.baseline_control: No experiment modifying the meta-agent improver
claims.result_denominator: No higher-order trial or comparable-budget improver outcome
claims.counterevidence: Meta-agent prompts remain fixed; growing context is not demonstrated algorithm-level improvement.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Architecture search with retained artifacts, not observed improver-level recursive improvement.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Fixed-meta-agent offline code search produces reusable agent workflows with author-reported later-task and cross-executor gains, strongest in math and DROP. Not uniform transfer dominance, isolated archive causality or improver-level self-improvement.
unresolved: Independent FunSearch/OPRO originals; archive-off compute control; cross-search seed variation; source-test ranking and benchmark family overlap; displayed-code reproducibility discrepancy.

reason: Full supplied text supports in-scope offline execution-feedback code search, archive persistence and held-out reuse. Central transfer claims require qualification; higher-order self-improving designer is future work, not an improver-level result.
rationale: 整段工作流代码经执行评分搜索并留存，跨任务与模型复用证据较强；但无等预算档案消融，ARC按测试选优，跨搜索方差和部署成本不足。
